This WWII vessel provides a rare glimpse into maritime history, inviting visitors to explore its corridors and imagine the stories of valor that resonate within its walls. The juxtaposition of the tranquil garden settings against the rugged exterior of the submarine creates an engaging atmosphere that is both educational and reflective. Visitors can wander through the well-maintained paths of vibrant flora, offering a perfect respite for those seeking nature’s tranquility amidst the historical significance of the park. A visit during seasonal blooms will awaken your senses with an array of colors and scents, all while the rich history of the USS Batfish looms nearby, ready to be uncovered. The contrast between the serenity of the botanical spaces and the powerful presence of the submarine ensures a memorable and engaging outing. Families, history enthusiasts, and nature lovers will find much to appreciate as they immerse themselves in the beauty and bravery that this unique park has to offer. **Muskogee War Memorial Park** promises an enriching experience for all ages—a true testament to the duality of life and its histories entwined in nature and valor. It’s not just a park; it’s a living tribute that celebrates both the past and the present, making it a must-visit destination on your trip to Muskogee.

museums.content_description:
**The National Cowboy & Western Heritage Museum** stands as a testament to the enduring legacy and culture of the American West. Located in Oklahoma City, this museum houses a remarkable collection of over 28,000 artifacts that vividly tell the story of cowboy life, Western art, and Native American heritage. As you step inside, you’re greeted by the intricate architecture that mirrors the rugged beauty of the West, featuring stunning sandstone walls and expansive galleries filled with natural light that enhance the experience of each exhibit. From historical artifacts to modern Western art, every corner of the museum resonates with the essence of the frontier spirit.  

One of the museum's standout features is its collection of Western art, including works by renowned artists like Frederic Remington and Charles M. Russell. These masterpieces capture the unparalleled landscape and diverse personalities that defined the era. The museum also offers immersive experiences for visitors, such as the live demonstration of traditional cowboy skills or curated exhibitions like 'The State of Craft', showcasing contemporary artisans who draw inspiration from Western themes. You can stroll through the beautifully landscaped gardens or visit the Hall of Great Westerners, which honors those who have significantly impacted Western history. Whether you're a history enthusiast, an art lover, or simply curious about cowboy culture, the **National Cowboy & Western Heritage Museum** promises an enriching experience that pays homage to one of America's most captivating chapters.  

Be sure to visit during unique exhibitions, like the upcoming *Alicia Kelly: Roughly Right* or *Shawn Smith: Entangled Ecologies*, providing fresh insights into the intersection of art and Western culture. This museum is a vibrant celebration of the West, a journey back in time that visitors of all ages will find inspiring and memorable.

There are several activities around the grounds to do such as: visiting the museum, taking photos with Santa and Mrs. Clause (lobby of museum), going to the Petting Zoo, riding in the hayride (pick-up is outside the barn of petting zoo), and so much more.

I will suggest from personal experience to go on the hayride first then to the museum for photos of Santa afterwards as the lines will typically be shorter in that order. In the year's I have attended, I've noticed people going to visit Santa first and exploring the museum so the noise and crowds can become overwhelming indoors. If you do the hayride and petting zoo first, it gives time for the museum to clear out. On the years I haven't done the hayride first, the line has taken 45mins-1 hour to get on and depending on weather it may be freezing outside. So trust me when I say to go in reverse order! Hayride then photos with Santa.

I, however, do not recommend going to the cafe for concessions or to the cabin for hot chocolate and cookies as those lines can be long as well... there's just so much to do that if you spend your time in line here, you'll miss out on everything else. But to each their own. It's not my family's preference though.  Every year it's the been the same, overly packed jammed full.

Overall, I highly recommend visiting Woolaroc during the holiday season. There will be a crowd no matter the day you attend over the weekend but it is still well worth the experience!

Tucked away on the picturesque shores of Grand Lake, this open-air museum invites you to stroll through time, experiencing the sights and sounds of a self-sustaining community. From the charming blacksmith shop to the rustic schoolhouse, each building in the village is filled with carefully curated items that echo the craftsmanship and ingenuity of earlier generations. Visitors can get up close with an extensive collection of antiques, farm implements, and tools, evoking a sense of nostalgia and wonder. 

As you walk through the village, you’ll appreciate its enchanting landscape adorned with lush gardens and beautiful walking paths, perfect for family outings or solo explorations. The museum also hosts a variety of seasonal events and special exhibitions, such as the upcoming **State of Craft 2025** and art showcases by contemporary artists like Alicia Kelly and Shawn Smith, blending traditional craftsmanship with modern interpretations. With engaging educational programs and hands-on activities, **Har-Ber Village Museum** provides visitors not just a look but an experience—one that connects the past to the present, igniting a passion for history and heritage in all who visit.
content_highlights: Over 100 authentic historical buildings representing early Americana
Extensive collection of antiques, tools, and artifacts from the 19th and 20th centuries
Engaging seasonal events and art exhibitions featuring contemporary artists
Beautifully landscaped grounds with walking paths and gardens
Interactive educational programs for visitors of all ages

museums.content_description: **Gilcrease Museum** stands as a unique beacon of American art and history in the heart of Tulsa, Oklahoma. Founded by oilman Thomas Gilcrease in the 1940s, this museum houses one of the most comprehensive collections of *American Western art*, featuring over 20,000 objects that span multiple centuries. As you wander through its galleries, you'll encounter masterpieces by iconic artists such as *Frederic Remington* and *Georgia O'Keeffe*, each piece telling a story of the American experience and spirit. The museum's dedication to preserving the culture, history, and heritage of the American West is palpable in every exhibit. From historical artifacts to contemporary works, there's something for every visitor to appreciate and enjoy.  Additionally, the surrounding gardens are meticulously landscaped and provide a serene backdrop, encouraging reflection on the artworks and their histories.  Beyond the art, the museum also delves into Native American history, showcasing significant collections that illuminate the lives and stories of indigenous peoples throughout time.  Visiting **Gilcrease Museum** not only allows you to witness influential works of art but also to engage deeply with the narratives that shaped a nation. With curated exhibitions and interactive programs, it’s a vibrant hub for learning and discovery.  Whether you're an art aficionado or a casual traveler, your experience will be enriched by the diverse offerings of this exceptional museum.

museums.content_description:
**Philbrook Museum of Art** is one of Tulsa’s essential stops for art lovers because it offers more than galleries: it’s a complete aesthetic environment. Housed in a historic villa with **Italian Renaissance-inspired architecture**, the museum’s sequence of elegant interior rooms and garden-facing vistas creates a visit that feels part museum, part cultural retreat. The setting encourages slow looking—moving from intimate galleries to dramatic views across terraces, reflecting pools, and formal plantings that echo the building’s symmetry and classical proportions.

Inside, Philbrook shines as a regional art museum with a strong traveler-friendly rhythm: **seasonal exhibitions** and focused projects that spotlight material intelligence and contemporary ideas. Upcoming programming points to this emphasis—*The State of Craft 2025* foregrounds the artistry of making, while solo presentations like **Alicia Kelly: Roughly Right** and **Shawn Smith: Entangled Ecologies** suggest a commitment to artists engaging with process, environment, and experimentation. For visitors, this means there’s often something new to discover even on repeat trips, with shows that reward close attention to texture, technique, and concept.

Plan your visit as you would a great house-and-gardens experience: arrive early, move through the galleries, then return outdoors to let the art resonate in the landscape. The museum’s architecture and gardens are not just a backdrop—they’re part of the aesthetic argument, making Philbrook a memorable destination for anyone who enjoys *craft*, contemporary practice, and art experienced through place.
